notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood to reduce live-agent load via high-volume chat deflection. Primary goal: push 65-80% of low-complexity chats to automated flows without increasing latency or failing under EOD spikes. Cost sensitivity is primary — measuring unit economics per session/token vs current vendor.

Background/context: Convergent Pulse runs a multi-tenant chat platform for telco & retail customers. Peak concurrency ~18k chats / day, 2.5M messages/month. Prior experiments with off-the-shelf LLM API were fast but expensive; on-prem quantized models showed lower cost but operational headaches.

Requirements (from product & infra):
- Workloads: high-volume synchronous chat, quick ticket summarization on create/close, agent assist snippets (suggest replies, triage tags), and automated tool-calling for order lookups.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 450ms for short-turn message (user->bot), end-to-end < 1.2s desirable.
- Throughput target: sustain bursts up to 3x baseline for 30-45min windows.
- Cost target: reduce per-session inference spend by >= 40% vs current managed vendor; target ARR/TCO constraints in linked drive doc.
- Model preferences: open Llama-family variants and 8-bit/4-bit quantized backfill for cheap routing; fallback to larger model only on hallucination risk.
- Routing/fallback: need smart routing by cost tier + semantic similarity to cached prefixes, prefer prefix caching for common intents.
- Reliability: automatic region fallback and model-variant fallback; prefer caching/KV reuse across multi-turn.

POC status & timeline:
- Jan 2026: initial call, shared usage logs and prompt inventory.
- Feb 18 2026: POC kickoff (Fireflies attached). Core hypothesis: batching + prefix caching + 4-bit quantization yields 45-60% cost saving w/ <10% latency impact.
- Feb 24 2026: ingest sample traffic, built representative prompt set, measured seq-length distribution (median 48 tokens user, 80 token response).
- Mar 01 2026: Redwood provided baseline perf numbers on hosted_api and ded. Redwood Optimize suggested batching window 20-40ms and prefix cache TTL 12 hours for their workload.
- Mar 05 2026: internal cost model updated. Need Redwood to run a short spike test (48h) and provide token-level cost breakdown.

Conversations notes (shorthand):
- "We need predictable unit economics — finance will greenlight if per-session cost halved or predictable with caps." — Head of Ops
- SE feedback: prefer dedicated capacity if variance in SLA can't be guaranteed on hosted.
- Security: must support SSO + audit logs + KMS; customer data retention policy 90 days, some customers require EU residency.

Open technical questions for Redwood:
- Can Redwood run transient burst test with 3x concurrency and provide token-level cost + latency heatmap?
- How does automatic batching interact with tool-calling and function/tool-response latency? Need safe timeouts for upstream systems.
- Quantization profile: do 4-bit runs keep acceptable hallucination rates on extraction tasks (order numbers, invoice ids)?
- How easy to pin routing policies per-customer (retail vs telco) in the same tenant?

Next immediate steps:
- Redwood SE to provision short spike POC (48h) on a representative model and return token-level billing + latency breakdown by Mar 20.
- Convergent Pulse will sign NDA addendum for KMS tests and provide a small EU-region sample to test data residency.
- Schedule exec pricing call w/ VP Revenue week of Apr 6.
